A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Relightable Holoported Characters work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-subject relighting experiments, quantitative baseline comparisons, component ablations and qualitative results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds runtime, memory, tracking-error and further ablation results in Appendices K–L.

M1.justification: The character animation, physics-informed features, AlbedoNet, RelightNet architecture, Gaussian rendering and training losses remain unchanged. The added feature-removal and few-shot fine-tuning trials evaluate variants of the existing model.

E1.justification: The five captured subjects and existing lighting domains remain unchanged. Appendix L adds cross-identity few-shot adaptation from Subject 2 to Subject 5 as an evaluated task, extending coverage within the existing dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains R4D, R4D + GT Env., IA + GT Env., MA + GT Env., HPC and HPC + NG. The new runtime comparison uses existing comparator families; the additional related-work citations do not introduce evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: Appendices K–L add component timing on an H100 excluding data loading, tracking evaluation using MPJPE, joint two-view tracking and image input, and adaptation using 12 Subject-5 samples for 1,000 iterations with selected blocks updated. The original splits, accuracy metrics and main training protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix L adds targeted tests removing all physics-informed features, combining two-view tracking with two input views, and adapting across identities (Table 6, Figure 15). Appendix K adds component profiling. These extend the existing component, view-count, lighting-diversity and robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix K newly specifies that component runtimes are averaged over 100 iterations. This adds timing-repetition and aggregation information, without establishing additional independent training runs. Neither version reports accuracy confidence intervals, seed variability or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds PSNR results of 29.68 without all features, 27.82 with two-view tracking and 29.07 for few-shot adaptation. Tables 4–5 add runtime and memory measurements, including 0.51 seconds and 49,884 MB for the full method; Appendix L adds 18.54 mm tracking MPJPE. Tables 1–2 and the renumbered lighting-diversity results are unchanged, so these are additional results rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, including rendering, deformation, cross-attention, Gaussian projection and training losses, are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: sparse-view dynamic human relighting, RelightNet with physics-informed features, and the interleaved lightstage capture strategy and dataset. The additional experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 identifies Sapiens normal estimation as the main runtime bottleneck, attributes few-shot artifacts to source-subject material and UV bias, and discusses improved tracking or pose priors as requirements for stronger two-view performance. These refine the existing runtime and identity-generalization limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds RelightNet's approximately 27 million parameter count, profiling conditions, Open3D/OptiX timing alternatives, and the precise blocks and budget used for adaptation. Existing architecture, capture and main training details remain intact; the project link and planned dataset release are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a brief scope-setting sentence acknowledging non-relightable animatable avatars and free-view human rendering, accompanied by 12 additional references. The substantive positioning against human-relighting research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the appendix overview, shortens two appendix headings, adds runtime and further-ablation sections, moves Additional Qualitative Results from K to M, and adds acknowledgements. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact tables for profiling, baseline resource comparisons and further ablations, plus Figure 15 showing the new ablations. The previous lighting-diversity table becomes Table 7, and Figures 15–16 become Figures 16–17. Existing figures and the overall layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes practical applicability easier to assess: Tables 4–5 quantify computational costs beyond v1's approximate 2 FPS statement, while Table 6 and Figure 15 provide evidence about tracking and cross-identity limitations. These improve transparency and empirical support without changing the main accuracy results. The benefit is bounded because the additional studies are targeted, including only one reported identity-transfer setting.
